incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency > 6s for model rwd-57 in eu-west-1 (detected 2026-03-20T09:14:04Z). paging nina (oncall).

 nina (oncall): acknowledging. I'm seeing an elevated tail on the stream router dashboards across three pods pinned to host gpu-node-18. p95 went 500ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~6.8s. Some clients report SSE disconnects and stalled chunks.

 kevin (support): two enterprise customers opened tickets mentioning resumed connections losing partial responses. Biggest impact: BoltAI (dedicated pool). They're hitting timeouts on long-lived streams.

 zach (ml-infra): pulling quick health: checking NVML and ECC metrics. grabbing `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi` now.

 yasmin (eng-runtime): logs from stream-router show repeated stall traces while flushing KV cache to GPU memory. snippet from router logs:

```
[2026-03-20T09:12:47Z] stream-router: flush_kv failed: timeout waiting on gpu lock (gpu-0), retrying
[2026-03-20T09:12:49Z] stream-router: stall: 3200ms waiting for device
[2026-03-20T09:13:05Z] runtime: session resumed token=abc123, offset=5421
```

 yasmin (eng-runtime): also capturing node-level syslog from gpu-node-18 showing multiple correctable ECC messages and a thermal event: `thermal_throttle: GPU0 power limit engaged`.

 arian (sre): ops runbook for hw degradation: mark node suspect, cordon + graceful drain, failover streaming routes, increase pool capacity, start hardware replacement if errors persist.

 incident-bot: Notifying arian (sre). Severity provisional: Sev2.

 nina (oncall): handing off to arian for mitigation. I'm leaving cluster queries in thread.

 arian (sre): taking over. immediate plan:
- mark gpu-node-18 as `suspect` in inventory
- taint node and evict streaming pods (graceful)
- route new sessions to fallback rwd-57-q4 (lower mem footprint)
- scale dedicated pool by +3 replicas for capacity
- notify infra to open HW ticket for GPU replacement

 zach (ml-infra): prometheus check in progress, query used:
```
sum(rate(streaming_request_duration_seconds_bucket{model="rwd-57"}[5m])) by (le)
```

 zach (ml-infra): pulled `nvidia-smi` for gpu-node-18:
```
index, temperature, utilization, ecc_corrected
0, 88 C, 97 %, 213
1, 44 C, 12 %, 1
2, 45 C, 15 %, 0
```

 zach (ml-infra): GPU-0 is hot and has growing correctable ECC counts. other GPUs look normal. mapping shows most streaming shards were scheduled onto GPU-0 due to previous shard affinity.

 yasmin (eng-runtime): quick mitigation: set `stream.resume_window` to 150s and enable resume tokens. Also will ramp session keepalive and increase router retry attempts for resume. Pushing config patch now.

 arian (sre): applying taint: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-18 rwd_degraded=true:NoSchedule --overwrite` then drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=45 --timeout=600s`

 arian (sre): initiated drain. note: streaming clients will re-establish; router resume token will reduce duplication.

 kevin (support): sending customer note: "We are actively mitigating a hardware issue affecting streaming response latency in eu-west-1. Traffic is being temporarily routed to fallback model variants and we are replacing a suspect GPU. We will provide another update in 1 hour."

 zach (ml-infra): after draining GPU-0, p99 for rwd-57 dropped to ~1.3s within 4 minutes, p95 ~370ms. streaming error rate down 80%. Progress looks good.

 arian (sre): opened hardware case HW-99012 for gpu-node-18. recommended replacement and full mem/ECC burn-in after swap. ops ticket linked.

 yasmin (eng-runtime): runtime follow-ups: implement a soft-rebalance to avoid shard-hotspotting and add per-GPU session cap to prevent single-device exhaustion. will propose PR with scheduler hint and a shard rebalancer job.

 nina (oncall): incident status: mitigations applied; routing diverted; severity downgraded to Sev3. leaving for follow-ups.

 ops-bot: Incident recorded as INC-2026-0320-09. Severity reduced to Sev3.

 arian (sre): post-mitigation actions assigned:
- zach: full ECC telemetry dump + node-exporter snapshot (due +3h)
- yasmin: PR for shard rebalancer and resume-window emergency toggle (PR +24h)
- ops: schedule GPU replacement and confirm closure (due +6h)
- kevin: customer follow-up and close support tickets (ongoing)

 kevin (support): will send combined timeline and attach logs once available.

 nina (oncall): confirmed no model integrity issues, no exfiltration. appears to be hardware-induced ECC + thermal power clamp causing long tail stalls. documenting logs in the incident page. :white_check_mark:

 arian (sre): recommend adding an alert: GPU correctable ECC rate > 50/min OR temp > 80C triggers paging. will add to alerting backlog.

 incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (automated): p99 returned to below threshold; routing restored to primary pool. Timeline and participants recorded.

 nina (oncall): thanks team. I'll draft a short postmortem and include recommended schedule for hardware swap and long-term mitigations.

 yasmin (eng-runtime): one more note: consider adding a rolling shard assignment run post-deploy to avoid immediate hotspotting on a single GPU when pods restart.

 zach (ml-infra): ACK, attaching prometheus snapshots to the incident doc.

 arian (sre): closing thread. reopen if regressions occur or new telemetry changes."
